title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
gist: Microsoft's Windows 11 preview adds a customizable right-click menu and Cloud Rebuild, while Windows OEM revenue fell 27 percent as PC demand weakens. Azure grew 48 percent.

insights.claim: Windows 11 preview update KB5127936 adds a 'customize menu' button letting users toggle, rearrange and control third-party commands in the right-click menu.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge

insights.claim: Cloud Rebuild reinstalls Windows 11 from the cloud via Windows Update without recovery media, but behaves like a fresh install since existing apps and files are not included.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge

insights.claim: Windows OEM revenue decreased 27 percent (28 percent constant currency), below expectations, due to prior-year Windows 10 end-of-support demand, OEM inventory drawdowns and weaker PC demand.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: PC market softness is a headwind for Windows OEM and PC hardware vendors.
insights.quote: Windows OEM revenue was below expectations

insights.claim: CFO Amy Hood expects the declining Windows OEM trends to continue through the rest of the fiscal year, and the broader Windows OEM and devices category fell 22 percent.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge

insights.claim: Azure grew 48 percent and Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30 percent, now roughly 70 percent of $92.3 billion quarterly revenue.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Microsoft's growth is cloud-driven while Windows licensing shrinks.

insights.claim: New hardware efforts such as the Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark platform came too late in the quarter to register in results.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Hardware refresh could help in later quarters.
